description: MTEngineSDL capability vocabulary. THE single source of truth for the capability list, defaults, implications, dependencies, licences and symbol patterns. The engine owns this file; apps own only their mtengine.caps manifests. Adding a new app is a manifest, never a patch here.

core.description: Always-on libraries that belong to no capability. They must appear in LICENSES.txt: a document derived from the resolved capability set alone is legally incomplete while looking complete.

MT_CAP_LLM.description: Local large-language-model inference via llama.cpp, plus model discovery and download.
MT_CAP_LLM.implies_note: HTTPS, not merely HTTP, and it is settled rather than assumed: CLlamaModelManager.cpp:228 builds EVERY model URL as https://huggingface.co/..., and httplib::Client on an https:// host without TLS support fails at runtime. LLM=1 HTTPS=0 would build, link and be unable to fetch any model -- the succeeds-and-lies shape #3.4 abolishes. There is no plain-HTTP model source in the tree, so splitting the downloader would buy a configuration nothing uses.
MT_CAP_LLM.app_visible_note: No app guards on MT_ENABLE_LLAMA_CPP. Measured by grepping all four app src/ trees.
MT_CAP_LLM.acquisition_note: No Linux entry: platform/Linux/build-llama-cpp.sh was named here but has never existed. On Linux llama.cpp is built IN-TREE by the engine's own CMake (add_subdirectory(other/lib/llama.cpp), CMakeLists.txt:428), not acquired into the keyed deps bucket. Found 2026-09-03 by the L16 gate test, which checks that every acquisition path resolves to a file.

MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK.description: Video decoding and playback: FFmpeg, libvpx, opus, nestegg, and the platform hardware decoders.
MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK.app_visible_note: MT_ENABLE_FFMPEG appears in Video/CVideoSourceFFmpeg.h:10, a header app TUs include, AND one host app guards on it 40 times in its own src/. Both routes to app-visible are exercised by this one flag. MT_ENABLE_WEBM_VPX (added 2026-08-31, unification plan Phase 2) gates the legacy nestegg/vpx/opus lane -- CVideoSourceWebMVpx compiled unconditionally before, which made MT_CAP_VIDEO_PLAYBACK=0 an engine-blocked configuration: the link died on opus_*/vpx_* against the stub archive.

commercial.note: NOT a whole-capability veto. Video playback stays fully on and a decoder SET is withheld. A boolean field would describe none of this correctly.

ffmpeg.note: The FFmpeg decoder policy, in one place. Three build scripts used to carry their own copies of these lists -- and of the guard sets derived from them -- so a name added in one platform's script was invisible to the other two and to the licence scanner. What is NOT here, deliberately: FFmpeg's implicit selects (h263 arrives with mpeg4, its parser with mpeg4video) and the object-file names, which are facts about a pinned FFmpeg version rather than policy, and belong beside that pin in the scripts.
ffmpeg.decoders_withheld_note: Patent-encumbered, and withheld from every DISTRIBUTED build -- the public/free tier as much as the store tier, because patents attach to distribution rather than to payment. Present only when the resolved mode is `full`, which mtcaps gives only to MT_PRIVATE_BUILD=1. This list was commercial.forbidden_decoders_commercial until 2026-09-02; the licence scanners read it here now.
ffmpeg.parsers_note: A parser is not a decoder: hevc and aac parse in both modes because parsing a bitstream infringes nothing. Only the vc1 parser follows its decoder into full mode.
ffmpeg.demuxers_note: Identical in both modes -- asf demuxing is licensing-safe under Microsoft's Open Specification Promise -- and none select-depends on another demuxer.

MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS.description: Still-image codecs beyond the core set: TIFF, WebP, AVIF and HEIF.
MT_CAP_PHOTO_CODECS.app_visible_note: one host app guards on MT_ENABLE_LIBTIFF, MT_ENABLE_LIBWEBP (x2), MT_ENABLE_LIBAVIF and MT_ENABLE_LIBHEIF in its own format-support test. Decision E was reversed on this measurement.

dependencies.provenance: git clone (call sites Linux:293, MacOS:396, Windows:258)

dependencies.name: libjxl
dependencies.provenance: git clone + its own submodules highway/brotli/skcms (Linux:296, MacOS:398, Windows:399/:401)

dependencies.name: libheif
dependencies.licence: LGPL-3.0 (container); its HEVC decoder is the licence question
dependencies.version: system package on Linux today; vendored in #5.5a
dependencies.provenance: pkg_check_modules on Linux, ImageIO on macOS, absent on Windows

commercial.note: HEIF has no key of its own -- it lives under this capability -- so 'commercial mode turns HEIF off' CANNOT be capability-off, which would take TIFF, WebP, AVIF and RAW with it. It is the FFmpeg shape: the capability stays on and a decoder is withheld. Pending the #5.5a licence spike.

MT_CAP_RAW.app_visible_note: Measured: MT_ENABLE_LIBRAW appears in the four app trees only inside a COMMENT in one host app's init code saying the opposite. It joins the app-visible set if and when a grep finds a real guard.

dependencies.name: LibRaw
dependencies.licence: CDDL-1.0 or LGPL-2.1 (dual; the CDDL option is what makes a commercial build possible)

MT_CAP_DEVELOP.implies_note: Verified by the includes: Develop/DevelopMath.cpp:3 includes CRawDecoder.h. The WORK ORDER in #5.5 is the opposite direction -- gate RAW first, because a guard on DEVELOP written before RAW has a stub has nothing to degrade to.

MT_CAP_COLOR_MANAGEMENT.description: Colour-management engines and DCP profile handling (Color/). NOT ICC parsing, which is core: Libs/icc is on the render path with no third-party dependency, and conflating the two is a mistake this design made twice.

dependencies.name: Little CMS (lcms2)
dependencies.provenance: downloaded tarball (Linux/Windows), part of the image-codec bundle

MT_CAP_KTX2.needs_guard_first: Core/CKTX2Loader.cpp has NO preprocessor guard today and is consumed unconditionally by CImageData.cpp, so unlike every other capability here there is no existing off-path to switch on. It needs the CImageDataTIFF.cpp treatment -- guard the body, keep the header unconditional, keep the file in all three build lists, #else-stub the entry points -- before it can be gated at all.

MT_CAP_CAMERA.description: Live camera capture. c64d needs it for C64 Ultimate support (decision 5).
MT_CAP_CAMERA.off_path_exists: Core/CCameraCapture.cpp:3 already guards the platform factory on MT_CAMERA_CAPTURE_ENABLED and :17-21 falls back to new CCameraDummy(). The off-path is written and compiling.
MT_CAP_CAMERA.linux_extra: On Linux the define is not the whole story: CMakeLists.txt:916 compiles platform/Linux/src.Linux/CCameraLinux.cpp and :949 links v4l2, both unconditionally. Both move behind the capability. v4l2 is a SYSTEM PACKAGE, so decision H applies -- a Linux manifest asking for camera without it fails the configure naming the install command.

MT_CAP_NET_GAME.implies_note: Gating NET_GAME without these gates nothing, and its acceptance criterion then passes vacuously.

MT_CAP_HTTP.description: Plain HTTP client (cpp-httplib) and the shared file downloader.
MT_CAP_HTTP.ownership_note: MT_CAP_HTTP OWNS cpp-httplib. MT_CAP_LLM depends on it and must not own it: Tools/NetGame/CFileDownloader.cpp is a shared consumer independent of any LLM, so leaving httplib inside the llama.cpp submodule makes a plain HTTP-only app pay for a 598 MB dependency to download a file.

dependencies.name: cpp-httplib
dependencies.version: currently reached through other/lib/llama.cpp/vendor/cpp-httplib; #5.3 vendors it as an engine-owned dependency

MT_CAP_HTTPS.description: TLS for the HTTP client, via mbedTLS.
MT_CAP_HTTPS.app_visible_note: MT_ENABLE_MBEDTLS appears in Libs/httplib/httplib.h:21, a header app TUs include, and it changes httplib::Client's STRUCT LAYOUT. This is the ODR case: an engine built with it on and an app TU compiled with it off stack-allocate different-sized Clients. c64d exhibits it on macOS and Windows today.

MT_CAP_WEBSOCKETS.description: WebSocket server/client via uWebSockets on uSockets.
MT_CAP_WEBSOCKETS.phase_note: Gated in Phase 4, not Phase 3: the uSockets consolidation in #5.4b rewrites the same archive this capability gates, so gating it first would gate a copy that is about to move.

dependencies.name: uSockets
dependencies.version: VENDORED at other/lib/uSockets with a local ARM64 fix (listenAddr = NULL, src/bsd.c:484, :602). Pristine upstream leaves that pointer uninitialised -- cloning upstream over it silently produces a broken archive.
dependencies.provenance: vendored source, NOT a submodule and NOT a sibling checkout

MT_CAP_MUSIC_PLAYER.description: Music player and playlists. Used by one host app today.
MT_CAP_MUSIC_PLAYER.implies_note: It does NOT imply an AUDIO capability: audio is CORE and has no vocabulary key, so an implication onto it would make mtcaps exit 2 on an unknown key. The coupling is real and is stated here as prose: the music player needs the core audio path, which is always present.

MT_CAP_MIDI.description: MIDI input and output via rtmidi.

MT_CAP_GAMEPADS.description: Gamepad support: the SDL gamepad layer and Core/GamePads.

MT_CAP_UNDO.description: Undo/redo framework (Tools/Undo). Used by one host app today.
MT_CAP_UNDO.note: No third-party dependency, so this is a CODE-SIZE capability rather than an acquisition one -- which makes it the cheapest place to prove the guard machinery without any acquisition change.

MT_CAP_FTXUI.description: Terminal UI toolkit, linked and used directly by the app.
MT_CAP_FTXUI.app_visible_note: One host app guards on MT_ENABLE_FTXUI in six of its own sites, and in the `#if X` style -- so on a platform where the flag is defined nowhere the guarded feature is OFF, and a value-style normalisation turns it ON.
MT_CAP_FTXUI.naming_note: It keeps the library name deliberately. A dependency-only capability has no engine feature to abstract -- no engine source includes ftxui, verified zero hits in src/ -- so the app links ftxui's API directly and the library name IS the feature name. Renaming it MT_CAP_TERMINAL_UI would also collide with MT_CAP_TERMINAL, a different capability.

MT_CAP_CRASH_REPORTER.note: The off-path has precedent: it is already headless-aware ('CrashReporter: disabled (headless=1 ...)').

MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE.app_visible_note: Appears in three headers app TUs include, and all four apps' src/Tests/ guard on it. Renamed from ENABLE_IMGUI_TEST_ENGINE in Phase 1 -- do not emit both spellings. GUARD WITH #if, NEVER #ifdef: this flag is emitted as =0 rather than absent, and #ifdef is true for a macro defined as 0, so an #ifdef guard compiles app code in while the engine has compiled its half out. DummyApp (6 sites) and c64d (9) both had that defect until 2026-08-28. The eight vendored src/Engine/Libs/imgui_test_engine/*.cpp are guarded the same way and registered in that directory's MTENGINE_PATCHES.md -- without those guards MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE=0 does not build at all, because imconfig.h has already removed the hooks they need.
MT_CAP_TEST_ENGINE.conditional_headers_note: imconfig.h:150 is the dangerous one -- miss it and every test-engine hook compiles out with NO build error at all, so the suites go quiet rather than red.

dependencies.name: imgui_test_engine
dependencies.licence: Dear ImGui Test Engine licence (free for open source; commercial use requires a licence from Omar Cornut)

commercial.note: Decision 0.1 of the 2026-08-31 unification plan: a store build (MT_COMMERCIAL_BUILD=1) must not carry the test engine -- resolve turns this capability off as a commercial effect, so no app needs to know. Dev builds keep it. The Disco Hello free tier (turnover <= $2M) currently covers the maintainer, so this is belt-and-braces, revisitable.

MT_CAP_TERMINAL.description: Embedded terminal emulator: libtmt and GUI/Controls/CGuiViewTerminal. A different capability from MT_CAP_FTXUI.
